catalog_quote: [Shaul 1982, pp. 206-207] The minimal phonemic system for Esselen proposed by Shaul (1981a) is given in (1) ... In terms of basic consonants, vowels, consonant series, syllabic shape and stress, the following are impressionistically like Esselen in descending order of likeness: Costanoan, Uto-Aztecan, Proto-Chumashan, Proto-Yuman, Southern Cochimi, and Salinan. [p. 212, exhibit (1)] Esselen (Es) ... Syllable canon: CV; common root shapes: CV, CVCV, CVCVCV; stress: penultimate [same exhibit: Salinan ... stress: not predictable, phonemic; Costanoan (C): Mutsun ... stress: mostly morpheme-initial] [p. 215, (20) continued, Data Summary] 5. PENULTIMATE STRESS: Es, C, UA, Ch [Shaul 1998, UCPL 131, snippet] ... Almost all Esselen roots are of the shape (C)V; there are a few roots ending in a consonant ([pek] 'one', [awur] 'teeth') ... stress, it is usually penultimate. The domain of the stress rule may include suffixes. (4) [putú-ki] 'large' [yakí-s-ki] 'large' [ukxú-s-ki] 'small' [exé-noc] 'man' [Shaul 1981a, OPOL 10, snippet] ... penultimate vowel. This stress rule is underscored when one notes that certain exceptions (morphemes of two vowels but non-initial stress) have suffixes. (22) [yakís-kV] [putú-kV] [ukxus-kV] ... stress rule thus includes at least some suffixes in its domain, allowing a tentative definition of word boundaries
world_status: statement found in an open source

In terms of basic consonants, vowels, consonant series, syllabic shape and stress, the following are impressionistically like Esselen in descending order of likeness: Costanoan, Uto-Aztecan, Proto-Chumashan, Proto-Yuman, Southern Cochimi, and Salinan.3' -- verbatim as quoted (the compiler ellipsis skips the roster citations). (b) PDF page 7 = printed p.212, exhibit (1), left column under 'Essele…
new_statements.rule_in_words: In Shaul's reconstitution of Esselen from the documentary record, word stress falls on the penultimate syllable (roots are CV, CVCV, CVCVCV with CV syllables); he treats penultimate stress as an areal trait shared with Costanoan (Mutsun), Proto-Uto-Aztecan and Proto-Chumashan.
new_statements.exceptions: None mentioned; the statement is a one-line entry in a typological exhibit, with no discussion of how stress was inferred from the 18th-19th c. transcriptions (Henshaw, Pinart and Galiano mark accents) or of vowel/consonant length, which Shaul notes is uncertain for Esselen (p.207).
new_statements.domain_note: Domain not specified (presumably the word/root as recorded in isolation in the vocabularies). Esselen is extinct and known only philologically; the analysis rests on Shaul 1981a 'A phonemic analysis of Esselen' (OPOL 10) and is superseded by Shaul 1995 IJAL 61:191-239 and Shaul 2019, neither of which could be opened here.
new_statements.identity_note: Source treats Esselen (Huelel/Excelen, esse1238, ISO esq) as a single language reconstituted from all documentary sources (La Pérouse 1786 through Harrington 1930s); no dialect distinction is made for the stress statement (Shaul 2019 later distinguishes Western vs Eastern Esselen vocabularies).
